# Android device smoke fixture (V3.4f.1)

This deliberately small **external ARC project** is the target for the first
physical-device frame milestone. It has one persisted active camera, one MeshRenderer asset GUID, one graph-authored unlit
material, and one actual source texture.

The fixture stores the scene and project configuration here, but **copies**
the GLB, material, and JPEG (plus their original `.arcmeta` files) from
existing tracked ARC sample assets. It does not require the editor's in-memory
asset database or invented GPU handles. The fixture must be regenerated by
the same production `arc-cook` package path used by runtime builds.

## Local preflight

Configure ARC with `BUILD_TESTING=ON` and build both `arc-cook` and
`arc-android-device-smoke-verify`. Run:

```sh
ctest --test-dir out/build -R '^arc-android-device-smoke$' --output-on-failure
```

The integration test creates an isolated project, cooks an
`android-arm64-vulkan` ASTC target, packages it, runs the normal
`arc-cook verify`, then reads **all** named artifacts using
`package_artifact_reader`. The verifier runs the actual runtime-side
tagged-scene, conventional mesh, Material v4, texture manifest,
texture, and compiled-shader decoders without Vulkan or Android SDK.

It fails when any required source GUID/dependency, runtime payload, or
hash is unavailable or incompatible. It is *not* proof of GPU frame
presentation: that requires a physical Android device.

## Hardware acceptance (next PRs: #1128, #403)

After wiring the same cooked package into the APK, select a physical
arm64 Android device with Vulkan 1.2 support, install a Development APK,
and capture `adb logcat` scoped to `ARC` / `Android`.

Pass only when all of these are observed:

1. Distribution manifest verified and cooked catalog mounted.
2. Startup scene materialized, mesh/material/texture payloads decoded.
3. Renderer attaches to a Vulkan adapter; new renderer generation
   hydrates mesh/material/texture GPU handles.
4. Log event `DEVICE_SMOKE_FIRST_SCENE_FRAME_PRESENTED` appears.
5. A screenshot confirms a **visible textured mesh**, not only the clear
   graph, and no error/validation messages were logged.
6. Background/resume and surface recreation each emit a fresh first-scene
   milestone without stale handles (V3.4e lifecycle follow-up).

The one-shot marker is emitted **only after the backend reports successful
presentation of an extracted scene frame**. Clear-graph fallback cannot
produce it. The marker is intentionally not a screenshot/pixel test; the
hardware acceptance step must still verify visible geometry.

The Android APK currently uses its existing packaged-content asset
bootstrap. Producing and deploying a *project-specific APK* is tracked
in #403, and the editor one-click workflow in #411. Neither is claimed
complete by this fixture.
